newsitem.title: USA: Carnival will not contest Celebrity merger.
newsitem.headline: Carnival will not contest Celebrity merger.

text.p: Carnival Corp. ended its takeover bid for Celebrity Cruise Lines on Thursday, saying it will not offer more than rival Royal Caribbean International's increased proposal of $515 million.
"We are sorry that we did not have an opportunity to put something together with Celebrity," Carnival said in a news release.
"Nevertheless, we gave it our best shot, and we respect the decision that the Celebrity shareholders made regarding the future of the line," Carnival said.

Cruise-ship leader Carnival last week offered $525 million for Celebrity, one of the few remaining independent cruise companies owned by privately held Chandris Group and Overseas Shipholding Group Inc., to counter an agreed $500 million merger agreement with Royal Caribbean.
Royal Caribbean had agreed to pay both cash and stock for Celebrity and to assume $800 million in Celebrity debt, giving the deal a value of $1.3 billion.

Carnival also agreed to take on Celebrity's debts and said it might raise its $525 million purchase price if it could identify more value in the upmarket cruise line specialising in Caribbean and Alaskan trips.
Late Wednesday, Royal Caribbean and Celebrity's owners said they had reached a definitive merger agreement and that the purchase price was being raised.
Carnival had privately bid $510 million in cash for Celebrity in early June, Carnival said last week.
"We wish both Celebrity and Royal Caribbean good luck," Carnival said.
Carnival's stock rose 69 cents to $43.56, Overseas Shipholding gained 50 cents to $20.56 and Royal Caribbean rose $1.25 to $35.875, all on the New York Stock Exchange at midday.
